question: Can the frozen obstacle logit support parent-disjoint POSITIVE, VERIFIED_NEGATIVE and UNKNOWN evidence with bounded false-negative and false-positive rates plus nonzero two-sided coverage?

result.interpretation: No outer fold obtained a complete threshold pair. The low-score tail could not provide verified-negative evidence under the 1 percent per-parent false-negative cap, and five folds also lacked a high threshold satisfying the per-parent false-positive cap with required positive coverage. This is a ranking and conditional-reliability failure, not merely a threshold-choice failure.

decision.next_successor_scope: On the same consumed six-parent ARKit/TUM Development pool, freeze the R21 factor checkpoint and DepthART prior, compute RGB+K-only obstacle/support/boundary/depth observables before outcomes, and test one tiny factor-interaction obstacle head. Use nested parent-disjoint fitting and threshold calibration: inner out-of-parent predictions select POSITIVE and VERIFIED_NEGATIVE thresholds, then the outer held parent is scored once. Require the same per-parent false-negative and false-positive caps, nonzero two-sided coverage on at least half of outer parents, and strict coverage gain over frozen-obstacle-score-only calibration. No reducer, fresh source or task outcome is authorized.

claim_boundary: Consumed checkpoint-held Development evidence that scalar threshold calibration of the frozen obstacle logit cannot safely supply two-sided obstacle evidence. It authorizes one small factor-interaction observability canary only; it does not establish a new model, task utility, independent cross-sensor generalization, deployment, product readiness, default-App eligibility, navigation utility or assistive safety.
